name: Webb Bridge Park
desc: 109-acre park with sports fields, a lake, an arboretum and a crushed-limestone trail that loops about 1.7 miles along a creek.
about: Webb Bridge Park covers 109 acres off Kimball Bridge Road and mixes busy sports fields with quieter green space. It has three grass soccer fields, a synthetic turf multi-purpose field, four baseball fields and four tennis courts, along with concession stands for game days.

Away from the fields, a 1.5-mile walking trail, a lake and an arboretum with more than 20 tree specimens give the park a natural side. The arboretum represents upland hardwood forest, conifers and trees typical of moist ravines and bottomland.

Kids gravitate to the Webb Zone Playground, and there is outdoor fitness equipment, a Play Me Again piano and a Little Free Library. Dog owners can use the on-site dog park, which has separate areas for large and small dogs. Three picnic pavilions are available on a first-come, first-served basis.
tips: Picnic pavilions are first-come, first-served, so arrive early on weekends.
Use the separate small-dog area if your pup is shy around big dogs.
Walk the 1.5-mile trail past the lake and arboretum.

name: North Park
desc: 97-acre park with sports fields, a lake, a reflection garden, a 1-mile paved trail and the city's Adult Activity Center.
about: North Park is a 97-acre city park on Cogburn Road with a strong focus on sports. It has eight lighted softball fields, two synthetic turf multi-purpose fields, five lighted tennis courts and six pickleball courts, making it a regular stop for leagues and pickup games.

The park also has a quieter side. A walking trail circles past the lake, and the Rotary Reflection Garden offers a calm place to sit. Two playgrounds keep younger kids busy, and a Little Free Library is on site.

North Park is home to the city's Adult Activity Center and an Arts Building, so it draws visitors for classes as well as games. Two picnic pavilions are available, one first-come, first-served and one that can be rented for gatherings.
tips: Reserve the rentable pavilion ahead of a party.
Pickleball and tennis courts are lighted for evening play.
Visit the Rotary Reflection Garden for a quiet break.

name: Brooke Street Park
desc: 5-acre passive park behind City Hall with an arboretum, paved trail, stream, sculptures and a covered bandstand.
about: Brooke Street Park is a 5-acre passive park behind Alpharetta City Hall, along Haynes Bridge Road in downtown. A winding concrete path loops around an open lawn and a landscaped stream, making it an easy spot for a short walk.

The park doubles as an arboretum, with specimen trees and more than a dozen trees that flower in spring. Public art sculptures here are part of the Downtown Alpharetta Arts Walking Tour, and a covered bandstand on the lawn hosts local concerts and performances.

There are cornhole boards for casual play, and a small reflection garden sits between City Hall and the Fulton County Library. Restrooms are on the exterior ground floor of City Hall and in the parking garage across from the library, and free parking is available downtown. The park is open from dawn to dusk.
tips: Check the downtown events calendar for concerts at the bandstand.
Visit in spring when the flowering trees bloom.
Park in the free garage across from the library.

name: Rock Mill Park
desc: 20-acre park on Kimball Bridge Road with pavilions, an environmental education area and a popular Big Creek Greenway trailhead.
about: Rock Mill Park is a 20-acre city park on Kimball Bridge Road that serves as one of the main trailheads for the Big Creek Greenway. With on-site parking and restrooms, it is a practical place to start a walk, run or ride along the paved greenway.

The park is known for its green roof pavilion, and a smaller group pavilion is available first-come, first-served for family gatherings and celebrations. An outdoor classroom supports environmental education programs.

Because it is smaller and more natural than the city's sports parks, Rock Mill suits picnics and quiet time outdoors as much as greenway trips. From the trailhead you can head along Big Creek toward other access points such as Haynes Bridge Park or Northpoint Park.
tips: Use Rock Mill as a greenway starting point with parking and restrooms.
The small pavilion is first-come, first-served.
Look for the green roof on the main pavilion.

name: Union Hill Park
desc: City of Alpharetta park on 13 acres reached from Union Hill Road off Windward Parkway. It has an outdoor pop-up skate park, a covered roller hockey rink, a pavilion and concession stand available to rent, on-site parking and an access point for the Big Creek Greenway trail.
tips: Use the on-site parking as a starting point for the Big Creek Greenway.
Bring skates or a scooter for the skate park and covered rink.
Contact the city ahead of time about renting the concession stand.
about: Union Hill Park is a 13 acre City of Alpharetta park at 1590 Little Pine Trail, reached from Union Hill Road off Windward Parkway near the Fulton and Forsyth county line. The city lists it as an access point for the Big Creek Greenway, with on-site parking that makes it a convenient place to start a walk, run or bike ride.

The park is better known for wheels than for ball fields. It has an outdoor pop-up skate park and a covered roller hockey rink, so it draws skaters, scooter riders and hockey players looking for a smooth surface with some protection from sun and rain. A concession stand at the park can be rented for events.

The Big Creek Greenway connection is the other big draw. From here, the paved trail follows the creek through wooded stretches, giving families an easy way to add a stroll or ride to a visit to the skate area. Contact the city's recreation department to confirm current amenities and rental details before planning around them.

name: Cogburn Road Park
desc: Nearly 6-acre neighborhood park with an arboretum, pavilions and a Play Me Again piano.
about: Cogburn Road Park is a six-acre neighborhood park in the Crabapple area, sized for an easy outing with young kids. Its large playground has separate sections for ages 2 to 5 and 5 to 12, and a 0.2-mile concrete path makes a short loop through the grounds.

The park doubles as one of Alpharetta's arboretums, with seven labeled trees meant as a small living museum for education and enjoyment. A Play Me Again piano, part of the city's public art program, invites anyone to sit down and play.
Two small pavilions are available on a first-come, first-served basis and work well for family picnics or a simple birthday gathering with a few friends.
tips: Arrive early to claim one of the two first-come pavilions.
The playground has separate areas for toddlers and older kids.
Try the Play Me Again piano while you are there.

name: Waggy World Paw Park
desc: 1.5-acre fenced, off-leash dog park for well-behaved pups.
about: Waggy World Paw Park is the off-leash dog park inside Wills Park, covering about 1.5 acres off Wills Road in downtown Alpharetta. It is divided into three fenced enclosures so dogs can play with others their size.

The large-dog area, for dogs over 25 pounds, is wooded with pine straw and has agility equipment and ramps. The small-dog area, for dogs under 25 pounds, has mature trees, grass and pine straw, and a third area is open to dogs of all sizes and is fully shaded. Benches are spread throughout, and waste stations are provided.
Water spigots and bowls are in the large- and small-dog areas, but not in the all-dogs area. The ground is mostly natural, so expect some mud after rain. Hours are 8am to sunset.
tips: Bring water if you plan to use the all-dogs area, which has no spigot.
Expect muddy paws after rain on the natural ground.
Use the small-dog side for pups under 25 pounds.

name: Alpha Loop
desc: A paved urban trail linking Downtown Alpharetta and Avalon, about a mile each way, with public art and pocket parks along the route.
about: The Alpha Loop is Alpharetta's growing network of urban multi-use trails, designed to link Downtown, Avalon, the North Point area and Northwinds. The paths are 12 feet wide and open to walkers, runners and cyclists.

The best-known segment connects Downtown Alpharetta and Avalon in about a mile, so it is easy to walk between dinner downtown and shopping at Avalon. Another section of roughly a mile, from Old Milton Parkway to Northwinds Parkway, opened on June 1, 2024. It passes through woods and along streams, ducks under Westside Parkway in a tunnel and includes an overlook bridge.
Permanent outdoor sculptures line both trails, adding public art to the route, and the loop continues to grow as the city builds new sections.
tips: Walk the Downtown-to-Avalon segment, about a mile each way.
Try the Old Milton to Northwinds section for a more wooded route.
Look for the outdoor sculptures placed along the trail.

name: Alpharetta Farm at Old Rucker Park
desc: A 2-acre working farm with gardens, a greenhouse and an outdoor classroom.
about: The Alpharetta Farm at Old Rucker Park, also called Old Rucker Farm, is a working organic vegetable farm on Rucker Road run by the city's Community Agriculture Program. Visitors can follow walking paths through the growing areas, and community garden plots let residents raise their own produce.

The farm is a hands-on learning spot. It offers volunteer opportunities, educational workshops and seasonal programs for all ages focused on sustainable growing, including summer Farm Fun sessions on topics such as bees, herbs and bird watching.
It is open to the public seven days a week from sunup to sundown, making it an easy, low-key stop for families who want kids to see where food comes from.
tips: Check the city's program listings for Farm Fun sessions and workshops.
Ask about volunteer days if you want to help in the fields.
Visit in daylight; the farm is open sunup to sundown.

name: Silos Park
desc: Small one-acre park in the Crabapple area built around four historic grain silos. Historical photos and a display explain how the silos once stored grain for local farms, making it a quick stop for a bit of local history while visiting Crabapple's shops and restaurants.
tips: Plan a short stop; the park is about one acre.
Read the historical photos to learn how the silos were used.
Pair it with a stroll through Crabapple's shops and restaurants.
about: Silos Park is a one-acre city park on Crabapple Road built around four historic grain silos. The silos once held grain for the area's farms, and historical photos on site show what Crabapple looked like during its farming days.

It is a small, quick stop rather than a full outing, and it fits naturally into a visit to the Crabapple area. Take a few minutes to read the displays and snap a photo of the silos, then continue on to the nearby shops and restaurants.
Families with history-curious kids may find it a simple way to talk about how the land around Alpharetta was used before the suburbs grew up around it.

name: Topgolf Alpharetta
desc: Point-scoring golf games for every skill level, with food and drinks served to your climate-controlled bay. Open year-round.
about: Topgolf Alpharetta on Westside Parkway is a three-level venue with more than 100 all-weather hitting bays, where microchipped balls score themselves as you aim at giant outfield targets. Bays have cooling fans in summer and heaters in winter, so it runs year-round, and Toptracer games add variety. Clubs are provided, or you can bring your own.

Food and drinks are served from a full restaurant and sports bar, with more than 200 HDTVs around the venue. There is also a rooftop terrace, private event spaces, golf lessons and EV charging in the lot.
No golf experience is needed. Guests under 16 must be supervised by someone 21 or older at all times, and guests under 18 need a 21-plus guest after 9pm.
tips: Book a bay online ahead of busy weekend evenings.
Under-18 guests need a 21-plus adult after 9pm.
Ask about private event spaces for group outings.

name: Main Event Entertainment
desc: Bowling, laser tag, high ropes, billiards and a huge game room under one roof.
about: Main Event Alpharetta is a large indoor entertainment center on Davis Drive with a long list of activities under one roof. Guests can bowl, including VIP lanes, play laser tag, climb the Gravity Ropes course, shoot billiards, try virtual reality and miniature golf, or work through escape rooms, mini escape rooms and challenge rooms.

An arcade, shuffleboard, MultiBall and the Human Crane, where players are lifted to grab prizes, round out the options. An in-center restaurant serves shareable appetizers, handhelds, desserts and cocktails.

The center is set up for groups, with birthday party packages, corporate and team-building events, school outings and social bowling leagues. Tables in the restaurant can be booked ahead, and food can also be ordered online.
tips: Book bowling or a party online ahead of weekends.
Check the deals page for current specials.
Ask about leagues if you want to bowl regularly.

name: Fairway Social
desc: Sports simulators, a nine-hole synthetic-turf putting course, food, drinks and live music.
about: Fairway Social on South Main Street is an entertainment venue built around indoor sports simulators. Groups can play world-class golf courses or a variety of other games, from target challenges to zombie dodgeball, in bays that suit all ages and skill levels.

It also works as a restaurant and bar, with a full-service kitchen serving chef-driven menus and signature cocktails, plus live music and live sports on screens throughout the venue. It comes from the same group behind Roaring Social in downtown Alpharetta.

Walk-ins are welcome, but you can also book a bay online. On arrival, check in with guest services and staff will walk you to your bay with tips and safety basics. Hours run Monday through Thursday 4pm to 10pm, Friday and Saturday 11am to 11pm, and Sunday 11am to 9pm.
tips: Book a bay online for weekend evenings.
Check in at guest services when you arrive.
Weekday hours start at 4pm.

name: Roaring Social
desc: Speakeasy-style lounge with boutique bowling, live music, cocktails and dinner.
about: Roaring Social is a 1920s-themed social club on Milton Avenue in downtown Alpharetta. The entrance plays up the speakeasy idea, opening into a room with velvet touches, craft cocktails and a lively evening crowd.

Live music is a centerpiece, with performers on stage five nights a week covering music across the decades. Boutique bowling adds a game to the night, played on shorter lanes with smaller balls and heavier pins in the style of old social clubs.

The kitchen focuses on shareable plates and late-night bites, and the bar is known for smoked and stirred cocktails. Hours run Tuesday through Thursday 5pm to midnight and Friday and Saturday 5pm to 2am, and it is closed Sunday and Monday. A separate event sales line handles private parties.
tips: Make a reservation online, especially for Friday and Saturday.
Check the events calendar to see who is performing.
Call event sales at 678-250-0610 for private parties.

name: Adventure Air Sports
desc: Trampoline and family entertainment center with racing slides and virtual reality.
about: Adventure Air Sports is a family entertainment center at 10800 Davis Drive in the North Point area, in the same complex as The Cooler. Alpharetta's visitor bureau describes it as combining fun and fitness, with thirteen attractions designed for all ages.

FOX 5 Atlanta's 2024 report on the then-new center highlighted trampolines, basketball, racing slides and a ninja obstacle course under one roof. The visitor bureau also points to virtual reality experiences that put guests inside the game, so there is something for both younger kids and teens who want more of a challenge.

Visits are sold as general admission, and the center also offers birthday packages and group events for teams, schools and other organizations. Some days have been set aside for private bookings, so check the schedule before heading over, especially during school breaks when families tend to plan outings.
tips: Check the schedule before going, since some days have been reserved for private events.
Ask about birthday packages if planning a party.
Group events can be arranged for teams and schools.
hours: Mon-Tue closed; Wed-Thu 3pm-8pm; Fri 12pm-10pm; Sat 10am-10pm; Sun 12pm-7pm

name: Immersive Gamebox
desc: Private interactive game rooms with projection mapping and motion tracking; 60-minute sessions for groups.
about: Immersive Gamebox at Avalon offers private game rooms where the walls, floor and sound react as your team plays. Projection and motion tracking turn you into the controller as you work through interactive levels, with titles such as Floor Is Lava, Squid Game and Angry Birds.

Each box holds up to six players, and sessions run 30 or 60 minutes. Larger groups are split into several boxes that play at the same time. The games involve mild physical activity, no gaming experience is needed, and most access needs, including wheelchair access, can be accommodated.

Arrive about 10 minutes early to check in, and use the free lockers for your things. Birthday packages add time in a party area with pizza, and corporate packages include meeting space and food. Bookings within 48 hours cannot be rescheduled or refunded.
tips: Arrive 10 minutes early to check in and split into teams.
Book for six or fewer per box; bigger groups play in multiple boxes.
Changes are not possible within 48 hours of your booking.

name: Odyssey Escape Game
desc: Team escape rooms with hidden clues and puzzles.
about: Odyssey Escape Game runs private escape rooms on Alderman Drive, with a second location in Suwanee. Every game is booked for your group alone, and reservations are required.

The Alpharetta rooms lean on story and setting. Titanic: The Final Hour puts players on the sinking ship, The Nuketown Diner and Jack the Ripper: Solve the Mystery offer different themes, and Towering Inferno: Race the Flames is played only at the Alpharetta location.

The facility is set up for birthday parties and corporate team building, with a conference room for discussions before and after a game and a lounge where groups can relax. You can reach the Alpharetta location at 770-559-7548 or 678-358-4060.
tips: Book online in advance; reservations are required.
Towering Inferno is only offered at the Alpharetta location.
Ask about corporate packages that include the conference room.

name: Urban Escape Games
desc: Locally designed escape rooms near North Point where teams have one hour to find clues, crack codes and solve puzzles to get out of a themed room. It bills itself as the first escape game company in Georgia and is popular for family outings, date nights and corporate team building, with debriefs offered for company groups.
address: 20 Mansell Ct E, Ste 275, Alpharetta, GA 30076
tips: Book online ahead of time; every game is private.
Pick by difficulty rating; the saloon room is the toughest.
Call (678) 805-2189 to plan a corporate or group visit.
about: Urban Escape Games operates escape rooms in Alpharetta and Marietta, with sets, clues and puzzles built by its own in-house team. The Alpharetta location on Mansell Court East offers four private, 60-minute adventures for 2 to 8 players.

Lunar Station 7 sends players to a moon base to solve a crime, Escape from Tiki Island strands the team on a tropical island, and Pirates' Cabin is a hunt for hidden gold. High Noon at Crazy Chip's Saloon, set in the Old West, carries the highest difficulty rating of the four.
Rooms work for family outings, date nights and birthdays, and the company helps plan corporate outings and school or community group visits. Check your booking confirmation for arrival instructions.

name: The Velvet Note
desc: An intimate acoustic jazz listening room, open Thursday through Sunday, with national acts and a 1924 Baldwin baby grand.
about: The Velvet Note is a jazz listening room in Brookside Commons on Old Milton Parkway, next to Jersey Mike's. It presents touring and regional musicians in an intimate room designed for listening, with acoustics engineered by designer George Seldon.

It has a full restaurant and bar, and food is served on palm leaf wooden plates so the clatter of dishes does not compete with the music. The club says it has never charged a food or drink minimum. Guest attire ranges from smart casual to polished.
Shows run Thursday through Sunday. Thursday opens at 6:30pm, Friday and Saturday have sets at 7:30 and 9:30pm, and Sunday has shows at 7 and 9pm. Some Thursdays feature an open mic jam.
tips: Call (855) 583-5838 to reserve tickets and seats.
Choose the early or late set on Friday and Saturday.
Look for it in Brookside Commons next to Jersey Mike's.

name: Matilda's Under the Pines
desc: Bring-a-picnic outdoor music venue with live shows in spring and summer.
about: Matilda's Under the Pines, also called Matilda's Music Under the Pines, is an outdoor concert venue at 850 Hickory Flat Road in Milton, just north of Alpharetta. Owner MJ (Mary Jane) Potter grew the series out of Matilda's, her former Alpharetta art gallery, and the venue calls itself an outdoor listening room focused on the performance. It books local, regional and touring Americana roots musicians, and it was named a winner in the 2024 Best of Georgia Awards from Georgia Business Journal.

Guests bring their own dinner and drinks, so many arrive with coolers, picnic baskets and lawn chairs. Tables and chairs are first come, first served, though you can stop by on concert day to put your name on a table. Gates open an hour before showtime, and the crowd is asked to keep conversation to before the show or between songs.
Enter at the 7 Acres restaurant on Hickory Flat Road, where an attendant directs concert parking. The schedule and tickets are posted on the venue's website.
tips: Pack a cooler with dinner and bring lawn chairs in case tables run out.
Come by on concert day to reserve a table under your name.
Do not park in the 7 Acres restaurant lot; follow the attendant to concert parking.

name: Wills Park Equestrian Center
desc: A 50-acre equestrian facility inside Wills Park with a covered arena and four outdoor rings, hosting horse shows, rodeos and dog shows year-round.
about: The Wills Park Equestrian Center occupies about 50 acres within Wills Park in downtown Alpharetta. The grounds include one covered arena, four outdoor rings, a 2.5-acre event lawn and nearly 30 horse stalls, plus show offices, concessions and restrooms.

Events run throughout the year, including horse shows, rodeos, concerts and dog shows, so the center draws both riders and spectators. Look for the equestrian-themed Play Me Again piano, part of the city's public art program.

The city and the Wills Park Equestrian Foundation broke ground on a revitalization of the facility in November 2021. Because events are scheduled by outside organizers, check the calendar before you visit to see what is on.
tips: Check the event calendar before visiting; the schedule varies.
Concessions and restrooms are on site during events.
Combine a visit with a walk around the rest of Wills Park.

name: RiverPines Golf
desc: Public 27-hole golf facility, including a separate par-3 course, on the Johns Creek border.
address: 4775 Old Alabama Rd, Johns Creek, GA 30022
about: RiverPines Golf is a public facility on Old Alabama Road in Johns Creek, just over the Alpharetta line, set along the Chattahoochee River. Its 18-hole course has five sets of tees for all skill levels, Bermuda fairways and bentgrass greens.

A separate 9-hole par-3 course, recently renovated, measures 951 yards and is built in a links style with tricky, sloping greens that reward a good short game. Practice facilities include a full driving range plus chipping and putting greens.

Instruction is a big part of the operation, with group and private lessons, adult clinics and junior programs, including a junior and high school league. Tee times can be booked online, and the website posts the current lightning status during storms.
tips: Book tee times online ahead of weekend mornings.
Check the lightning status page before heading out on stormy days.
Try the par-3 course to sharpen your short game.

name: Alpharetta Farmers Market
desc: Saturday-morning market on the Town Green, April through November, with local growers, bakers, makers and flowers.
about: The Alpharetta Farmers Market sets up on the City Center Town Green at 2 Park Plaza on Saturday mornings, from 8:30am to 12:30pm. The 2026 season runs from April 4 to November 14, with the market closed on October 10.

Vendors include local farmers, bakers, makers and artisans, so a typical visit means browsing fresh produce alongside flowers, baked goods, handcrafted items and treats. Some vendors offer samples and drinks as you walk the rows.

The market is directed and managed by the Alpharetta Business Association, and the City of Alpharetta posts weather-related updates. Because it sits in the heart of downtown, it pairs easily with coffee or brunch nearby and a stroll past the Town Green fountain and City Hall.
tips: Arrive early for the best selection of produce and baked goods.
The 2026 season ends November 14, and there is no market on October 10.
Check the city's updates on rainy Saturdays before heading out.

name: Alpharetta Food Truck Alley
desc: Ten or more food trucks and live music on Old Roswell Street, the fourth Thursday of each month from April through October. Bring a chair.
about: Alpharetta Food Truck Alley brings more than 10 food trucks to Old Roswell Street in downtown Alpharetta on the fourth Thursday of each month, from 5pm to 9pm. The cuisines change from month to month, and live music plays each evening, giving it the feel of a casual neighborhood street party.

The 2026 season ran from April through October, with dates on April 23, May 28, June 25, July 23, August 27, September 24 and October 22. The event is family-friendly, but pets are not welcome, so plan to leave dogs at home.

Seating is limited, so bring a blanket or a folding chair. Old Roswell Street and the adjacent lot close at 1pm on event days, and parking is available in the public decks at 92 Milton Avenue and 2 Park Plaza.
tips: Bring a chair or blanket, since seating is limited.
Park in the decks at 92 Milton Avenue or 2 Park Plaza.
Leave pets at home; they are not allowed at the event.

name: Alpharetta and Old Milton County History Museum
desc: Free museum inside City Hall telling Alpharetta's story from Cherokee territory through its years as the Milton County seat to today's tech economy.
about: The Alpharetta and Old Milton County History Museum is a free museum inside Alpharetta City Hall at 2 Park Plaza. Its exhibits trace the city's story from its time as Cherokee territory to its growth into a center for technology companies.

A large part of the collection covers 1858 to 1932, when Alpharetta served as the seat of Milton County. That county took in what are now Johns Creek, Milton, Mountain Park, much of Roswell and northern Sandy Springs, so the museum offers context for the whole north Fulton area.

Photos, memorabilia and artifacts come from residents and the Alpharetta and Old Milton County Historical Society. A stories kiosk plays interviews with about 70 local residents. The museum keeps weekday hours only, and it pairs well with the self-guided downtown History Walk.
tips: Admission is free; visit on a weekday, since there are no weekend hours.
Spend time at the stories kiosk with resident interviews.
Follow up with the self-guided downtown History Walk.

name: Alpharetta Arts Center
desc: 10,000-square-foot center on Canton Street with a black-box theater, visual arts and clay studios and rotating gallery exhibits.
about: The Alpharetta Arts Center is a 10,000-square-foot city arts facility on Canton Street in downtown Alpharetta. Inside are a black-box theater, visual arts and clay studios, a digital media studio and gallery space for rotating exhibits.

The center runs classes through the city's recreation program, with clay offerings that have included open studio drop-in sessions, hand-building and wheel-thrown pottery. Art events and exhibit openings round out the calendar.

Look for the Play Me Again project's upcycled baby grand piano, which the city describes as the first of its kind in the program. The building was designed by Houser Walker Architecture, and its location on Canton Street puts it within an easy walk of downtown restaurants and shops.
tips: Register for clay or art classes through the city's online class portal.
Check the events calendar for gallery openings and performances.
Combine a visit with dinner on Canton Street.

name: Mansell House and Gardens
desc: A 1912 Queen Anne home and gardens, home of the Alpharetta & Old Milton County Historical Society; tours by appointment and a popular wedding venue.
about: Mansell House and Gardens is a 1912 Queen Anne style home on Old Milton Parkway that serves as the home of the Alpharetta and Old Milton County Historical Society. The nonprofit traces its roots to a 1979 meeting and works to collect and preserve the history and genealogy of Alpharetta and old Milton County.

The house is best known as a rental venue for weddings, receptions, rehearsal dinners, showers, birthday and holiday parties, and meetings. Guests can use the wide porch, the gazebo and the interior rooms, and the gardens provide room for photos and a tent.

The society keeps office hours on Tuesday and Thursday from 9:30am to 1:30pm, and tours and planning meetings are available by appointment only. Its research archive is housed separately in the basement of the Log Cabin on Milton Avenue.
tips: Call 770-231-7160 to book a tour; visits are by appointment.
Office hours are Tuesday and Thursday mornings.
Use the society's research archive at the Log Cabin for family history.

name: Downtown Alpharetta History Walk
desc: Free self-guided walking tour with more than 20 historic markers spread through downtown Alpharetta, all within easy walking distance. The markers cover the industries that once drove the local economy and buildings that served very different purposes in the past. It suits all ages and is open year-round.
address: 178 S Main St, Ste 200, Alpharetta, GA 30009
tips: Pick up the free brochure at the Alpharetta Welcome Center.
Use the City Tours app if you prefer a map on your phone.
Visit the history museum in City Hall to round out the walk.
about: The Downtown Alpharetta History Walk is a free, self-guided tour built around more than 25 historical markers placed within walking distance of one another. Together they tell how the town grew, covering the industries that once drove the local economy and buildings that served very different purposes in earlier years.

You can follow the route with a complimentary brochure that also covers the Alpharetta and Old Milton County History Museum, available at the Alpharetta Welcome Center. The free City Tours app offers the same walk as a virtual guide, with each landmark pinned on a map, a short description and links to more background.

The walk suits all ages and works any time of year. Pair it with the free history museum inside City Hall for a fuller picture, and use it as a prompt to talk with kids about local and family history.

name: Walk of Memories
desc: Veterans memorial at American Legion Post 201 with nearly 8,000 engraved bricks honoring Georgians who served in every branch. Monuments mark World War II, Korea and Vietnam, and displays include a Cold War-era M60 tank, a UH-1 Huey flown in the 1968 Tet Offensive, a Navy twin 40mm gun and an Air Force T-33 trainer.
tips: Download the brochure from the Post's site before your visit.
Read the plaque near the Huey to learn the story of its mission.
Order a memorial brick through the Post for a $50 donation.
about: The Walk of Memories is a veterans memorial on the grounds of American Legion Post 201 on Wills Road. Close to 8,000 bricks along the walkway carry the names of Georgians who served in the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marines and Coast Guard, including those killed in action, those who died of wounds and prisoners of war.

Monuments spotlight conflicts including World War II, Korea and Vietnam, and seventeen Medal of Honor recipients are honored in one area. Large displays include a 93,000-pound M60 tank used in Europe during the Cold War, a UH-1 Huey helicopter flown in the 1968 Tet Offensive, a 40mm Mark 1 twin gun removed from the USS Polk County and an Air Force T-33 trainer.
Families can add a brick to honor a loved one for a $50 donation through the Post, and there is room for about 7,000 more.

name: North Point Mall
desc: Alpharetta's regional mall, anchored by Dillard's, JCPenney, Macy's and Von Maur. The city approved a major mixed-use redevelopment of the site in 2026, so expect changes in the years ahead.
hours: Mon-Sat 11am-8pm; Sun 12pm-7pm (department store, restaurant and theater hours may vary)
about: North Point Mall opened on October 20, 1993, and remains Alpharetta's regional enclosed mall, with roughly 1.3 million square feet of space near GA 400. Mall hours are Monday through Saturday 11am to 8pm and Sunday noon to 7pm, though department stores, restaurants and the AMC theater keep their own schedules. Anchors are Macy's, Dillard's, JCPenney and Von Maur, joined by stores such as H&M, Sephora, Aerie, American Eagle and Ann Taylor and the AMC North Point Mall 12 cinema.

Holiday hours for 2026: the mall is closed on Thanksgiving Day, Thursday, November 26, open 9am to 6pm on Christmas Eve, and closed on Christmas Day. Santa photos at the North Point Pole run from November 21 through December 24, and the mall's holiday kickoff is November 21.

Big changes are planned. In August 2026 the Alpharetta City Council voted 4 to 3 to approve the redevelopment of up to 100 acres of the site by Jamestown, the developer of Ponce City Market, with New York Life and The Machete Group. The plan centers on a 20,000-seat arena meant to host an NHL franchise, surrounded by an entertainment district and tied to a transit station on the GA 400 express lanes. Much of the deal depends on the NHL committing to an Alpharetta team by August 2031, and the mall remains open in the meantime.
tips: The mall is closed Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day, and closes at 6pm on Christmas Eve.
Department stores often open earlier and close later than the mall itself, so check the store's own hours.
Santa photos at the North Point Pole run November 21 to December 24.
title: North Point Mall Hours, Stores & Holiday Hours (2026) | Alpharetta
meta: North Point Mall in Alpharetta is open Mon-Sat 11am-8pm, Sun noon-7pm. Thanksgiving and Christmas hours, anchor stores, Santa photos and redevelopment news.

extraFaq.q: What are North Point Mall's holiday hours?
extraFaq.a: North Point Mall is closed on Thanksgiving Day (November 26, 2026), open 9am to 6pm on Christmas Eve (December 24), and closed on Christmas Day (December 25).

extraFaq.q: What stores are at North Point Mall?
extraFaq.a: Anchors are Macy's, Dillard's, JCPenney and Von Maur, with stores including H&M, Sephora, Aerie, American Eagle and Ann Taylor, plus the AMC North Point Mall 12 theater.
No closing date has been announced. The city approved a plan in August 2026 to redevelop up to 100 acres of the site around a proposed NHL arena, but the mall is open with regular hours.

extraFaq.q: When can you see Santa at North Point Mall?
extraFaq.a: Santa photos at the North Point Pole run from November 21 through December 24, 2026.

name: Sis + Moons
desc: Eclectic downtown shop on Milton Avenue mixing home goods, local art and vintage finds with candles and clothing. In back, The Treehouse at Sis and Moon's operates as a working studio and art gallery that hosts art classes, so the shop doubles as a creative hub in the downtown district.
tips: Ask about upcoming classes at The Treehouse studios.
Look for one-of-a-kind vintage pieces mixed in with local art.
Stop by Korner Soak a few doors away on Milton Avenue.
about: Sis + Moon's is an eclectic shop on Milton Avenue in downtown Alpharetta that showcases the work of more than sixty local artists. Shelves mix home goods, original art and one-of-a-kind vintage pieces, and local artists help curate items from both new and vintage sources.

The building is also a working creative space, with about twenty-five artist studios. The Treehouse at Sis + Moon's, also known as Treehouse Art Studios, operates as a studio and gallery and hosts art classes, so visitors may catch artists at work.

Its sister shop, Korner Soak, which focuses on bath and body products, is a few doors down on the same block. The shop's listed hours are Monday through Thursday 11am to 5pm, Friday 11am to 6pm, Saturday 10am to 6pm and Sunday noon to 5pm.

name: Korner Soak
desc: Small downtown Alpharetta shop specializing in bath and beauty products along with pajamas and loungewear. It comes from the sisters behind Sis + Moons and sits on the same stretch of Milton Avenue, making it an easy stop for cozy gifts, self-care items and soft layers while browsing downtown.
tips: Call ahead to confirm hours.
Pair bath products with loungewear for a ready-made gift.
Visit Sis + Moon's on the same block.
about: Korner Soak is a small, locally owned shop at 22 Milton Avenue in downtown Alpharetta. It specializes in aromatic bath and beauty products meant for relaxation and pampering, and it also carries pajamas and loungewear, so it covers both the bath and the cozy night in that follows.

Alpharetta's visitor bureau includes the shop in its Only in Alpharetta list of locally owned businesses. The mix of bath products and loungewear makes it a natural stop when you need a gift for a birthday, a hostess thank you or a self-care treat, and smaller items work well as stocking stuffers or add-ons to a larger present.

The store sits on the same stretch of Milton Avenue as Sis + Moon's, a short walk from Main Street and Alpharetta City Center, so it pairs easily with lunch or coffee downtown. Hours could not be confirmed, so call before a special trip.

name: Clothes Horse
desc: Menswear shop on Milton Avenue in downtown Alpharetta that bills itself as having north Atlanta's best collection of men's business casual apparel. Expect upscale casual shirts, trousers and layers for the office or weekends, with personal service from a small independent store.
tips: Call ahead to confirm hours.
Shop here for business casual basics and gifts for men.
Park once downtown and walk to the other Milton Avenue shops.
about: Clothes Horse Men's Apparel and Gifts is an independent menswear shop at 28 Milton Avenue in downtown Alpharetta. According to a BeLocal Alpha Milton Johns Creek feature, it is owned by Charleen Thompson, with her husband John Thompson, a former football coach, as co-owner.

Alpharetta's visitor bureau lists it for men's business casual apparel, with a curated collection of classic, comfortable clothing, premium accessories and gifts from established brands. BeLocal describes the look as upscale casual with a coastal style, and the shop also carries undergarments, with a back area holding a large assortment of additional items.

It is part of the cluster of independent shops and restaurants along Milton Avenue near the center of downtown, which makes it easy to pair with lunch or other errands. It suits anyone shopping for business casual basics, weekend wear or a gift for the men in their life. Call before visiting to confirm hours.

name: The Red Hound
desc: Gift and home decor shop at Alpharetta City Center that moved from its original Johns Creek location. It carries gifts for babies, kids, teachers, graduates, brides and hostesses, mixing one-of-a-kind pieces from local and regional artists with accessories and national brands.
tips: Stop in for baby, teacher or hostess gifts.
Look for pieces from local and regional makers.
Park in the City Center deck at 2 Park Plaza and walk over.
about: The Red Hound is a gift and home decor shop at 211 Market Street in Alpharetta City Center. It moved downtown from its original Johns Creek location when City Center added a group of new retailers in late 2018.

The shop is geared toward gift shopping for life's occasions, with items for babies, kids, teachers, graduates, brides and hostesses. Home decor and accessories fill out the space, and the owners work with local, regional and national brands to stock one-of-a-kind pieces.

Alpharetta's visitor bureau highlights its hand-picked finds, from whimsical accents to more thoughtful treasures, along with locally crafted fashion accessories. Its City Center address puts it steps from the Town Green, City Hall and the downtown parking deck, so it is easy to combine with lunch or a farmers market visit.

name: Comeback Vinyl
desc: Downtown vinyl shop with new and used records and a listening station.
about: Comeback Vinyl is an independent record store at 1 South Main Street in historic downtown Alpharetta, located next to the company's warehouse and offices for its national online shop. The brick-and-mortar store stocks a wide selection of new vinyl across many genres.

A built-in listening station lets you hear most records before you buy, and staff aim for a welcoming, no-judgment feel whether you are a longtime collector or just bought your first turntable. Online orders can be picked up at the store for free.

The shop also buys used LPs in playable condition, mostly music from the 1960s onward. Drop-offs need no appointment, offers usually arrive within a week, and store credit pays 10 to 15 percent more. Free street and deck parking is nearby.
tips: Test records at the listening station before buying.
Choose free in-store pickup for online orders.
Selling records? Drop off LPs with no appointment; store credit pays more.

name: Alpharetta Outfitters
desc: Downtown outdoor shop focused on fly fishing, with rods, reels, flies and gear alongside hiking and camping equipment and outdoor supplies. It also offers fly-fishing classes and guided trips, so it is a useful first stop for beginners and for anglers planning a north Georgia trout outing.
tips: Ask about a guided trip on the Chattahoochee.
Start with a curated beginner kit before buying piece by piece.
Visit Monday through Saturday; the shop is closed Sundays.
about: Alpharetta Outfitters on South Main Street is a full-service fly shop and a hub for anglers who fish the Chattahoochee River and the small trout streams of north Georgia. Gear on the shelves is vetted by the shop's professional guides, and starter kits make it easier for newcomers to get set up without overspending.

Beyond retail, the shop offers guided trips on local waters, instruction with fly-fishing teachers, and hosted travel packages to destination fisheries. Staff can also advise on gear and clothing for a trip, and the shop runs clinics and events listed in its newsletter.
A Reel Rewards program returns 5 percent on qualifying purchases. Store hours are Monday through Friday 10am to 7pm and Saturday 10am to 6pm, and the shop is closed on Sundays.

name: The Ginger Room
desc: Tea room in one of downtown Alpharetta's oldest buildings, serving traditional British high tea by reservation along with local and international loose-leaf teas. It is also known for all-natural ginger juices, including signature Ginger Yums in 17 flavors that can be mixed into more than 100 combinations.
tips: Reserve high tea ahead of time.
Pre-order fresh juice by the quart or gallon online.
The shop is closed Mondays.
about: The Ginger Room on Roswell Street in downtown Alpharetta is a juice, coffee and tea house best known for its high tea service, which is offered by reservation. The tea list includes local and international selections, including classic English teas from Fortnum and Mason and Harrods, and all teas are sold in take-home tins.

It is also home to Ginger Yums, an all-natural ginger juice that comes in 17 flavors and can be mixed into more than 100 combinations. Juice can be filled by the quart, half gallon or gallon and keeps about a week in the refrigerator. A separate Ginger Yums Sip Shop operates in Johns Creek.

The tea room hosts bridal and baby showers, birthdays and corporate events, and catering covers tea time to go, scones by the dozen and boxed lunches. It sources from local coffee roasters, bakers and artisans.

name: Queen of Hearts
desc: Large antique and home furnishings market on North Main Street, part of a group with Alpharetta, Buford and Marietta locations and more than 550 dealers in all. Booths carry vintage and antique furniture, lighting, decor, collectibles and sports memorabilia, plus DIY furniture paints and monthly workshops.
tips: Allow plenty of time to browse the many dealer booths.
Ask staff about upcoming DIY and furniture painting workshops.
Confirm hours before visiting.
about: Queen of Hearts Antiques & Interiors is a large antique and home furnishings market at 670 North Main Street in Alpharetta. Alpharetta's visitor bureau describes it as a well-loved stop filled with vintage pieces, collectibles and distinctive home decor.

The business was started by Stacey and Jim Anderson in the late 1990s with just 12 dealers and has grown to more than 550 booth spaces across its Alpharetta, Buford and Marietta stores, according to a City Lifestyle profile. Booths mix antique, vintage and new home interiors: furniture, lighting, area rugs, accessories, collectibles and gifts. Alpharetta dealers specialize in areas such as French and European antiques, farmhouse and rustic pieces, mid-century modern furniture and French Country decor, and some carry Dixie Belle chalk-style paint.
Expect a big space with many separate booths, so allow extra time to browse. The store has hosted frequent DIY workshops, and it has been open seven days a week.

name: Urban Hardware
desc: Large independent hardware, home and garden store on Haynes Bridge Road affiliated with True Value. Beyond tools, paint and repair supplies, it carries patio furniture, home and garden goods and seasonal holiday decor, with the hands-on service of a local store and a big-box sized selection.
tips: Bring torn window or door screens to be re-screened.
Ask about blade sharpening and key cutting while you shop.
Call ahead to check stock on grills, YETI gear or specific parts.
about: Urban Hardware is an independent hardware store at 11770 Haynes Bridge Road. According to a trade publication profile, it opened in April 2019 under owner Lee Pell and fills about 40,000 square feet, including a large garden center. Alpharetta's visitor bureau includes it among locally owned shops.

The selection goes well beyond basic tools. Expect power tools, cabinet hardware, lighting fixtures, paint and home decor, along with patio furniture, Carhartt workwear, premium grills and YETI gear. The garden center adds plants and outdoor supplies for seasonal projects.

The store also handles a range of repair services that many big box stores skip, including key cutting, blade sharpening, door and window re-screening, pipe cutting and threading, and glass cutting, plus help with minor home repairs. That makes it a practical stop for homeowners who want a part cut to size or a screen fixed rather than just a product off the shelf. Call ahead to check stock on a specific item.

name: Neese Heating, AC & Plumbing
desc: Locally owned since 1992, handling HVAC and plumbing with 24/7 emergency service.
about: Neese Heating, AC and Plumbing is a locally owned company founded in 1992 by Dewey Neese, a local resident, and based on Shiloh Road East. It handles repair, maintenance, replacement and installation of air conditioning, heating and indoor air quality systems, along with plumbing services, for homes and businesses.

Technicians are NATE-certified, and trucks carry a wide stock of parts with the goal of fixing most problems on the first visit. The company also performs home energy audits, using duct leakage, blower door and static pressure tests to look for wasted energy and ventilation issues.

Neese offers free estimates before work starts, 24/7 emergency service and a 100 percent satisfaction guarantee. Its service area includes Alpharetta, Johns Creek, Cumming, Canton, Holly Springs and Acworth.
tips: Ask for a free estimate before any work begins.
Call any time for emergency AC or heating repair.
Consider a home energy audit if some rooms stay hot or cold.

name: 4 Seasons Heating & Air
desc: Veteran HVAC company offering installation, repair and duct cleaning.
about: 4 Seasons Heating and Air is a full-service heating, cooling and indoor air quality company on Atlanta Highway that has served north metro Atlanta for more than 50 years. Its services cover AC and heat pump repair, installation and maintenance, furnace work, ductless systems, zone controls and thermostats.

Indoor air quality is a major focus, with duct cleaning, duct repair and sanitizing, air filtration and purification, humidifiers, dehumidifiers and UV lamps. The company also serves commercial customers and offers maintenance plans, financing and a free second opinion on installation quotes.

Repair and maintenance work is handled by NATE-trained technicians with stocked trucks. Office hours are weekdays from 8am to 5pm, with technicians on call on weekends and emergency service available. The company has received a Reader's Choice award for HVAC service in Forsyth County.
tips: Ask for the free second opinion on an installation quote.
Schedule service online or by phone on weekdays.
Weekend emergencies are handled on call.

name: Gagne Heating & Air Conditioning
desc: Residential and commercial HVAC with a Comfort Club maintenance membership.
about: Gagne Heating and Air Conditioning is an HVAC contractor based at 4095 Nine McFarland Drive in north Alpharetta. It serves homes, businesses, multifamily housing and new construction in and around Alpharetta and the greater metro Atlanta area, and it cites decades of industry experience. Carrier lists the company as a dealer and a past winner of the Carrier President's Award, the manufacturer's top dealer honor.

Services cover air conditioning and heating repair, tune-ups and replacement, heat pumps, ductless mini-splits, thermostats and emergency HVAC calls. Indoor air quality work includes air filtration, UV air purifiers and whole-home humidifiers and dehumidifiers, and a commercial team handles installation, repair and maintenance for businesses.

Its Comfort Club maintenance membership covers routine system care and, according to the company, adds priority service and discounts on repairs. Appointments can be booked online or by phone, and the company says it can often provide free same-day estimates for system replacements.
tips: Ask what the Comfort Club membership includes before your next tune-up.
Ask for a free estimate when replacing a system.
Book online if you prefer not to call.

name: Superior Indoor Comfort
desc: Residential and commercial HVAC and indoor air quality specialists.
about: Superior Indoor Comfort is a locally owned and operated heating and cooling contractor on Highway 9 North in Alpharetta that has been in business since 1993. The company describes itself as owner operated and rooted in Georgia.

Services cover the full range of residential and commercial HVAC work, including AC repair, heating repair, new system installations and preventive maintenance. Certified technicians handle both homes and businesses, with an emphasis on keeping systems running efficiently through Georgia's hot summers and cold snaps.

The company says comfort is more than a number on the thermostat, and it aims to make the whole service experience easy, from the first call to the finished job. For repairs, maintenance or an estimate, call 770-664-9098.
tips: Schedule maintenance before the summer and winter peaks.
Ask about both residential and commercial service.

name: Benjamin Franklin Plumbing of Alpharetta
desc: Locally owned 24/7 plumbing franchise serving Alpharetta and North Fulton.

about: Benjamin Franklin Plumbing of Alpharetta is a locally owned and operated franchise based on Union Hill Road that serves Alpharetta, Milton, Johns Creek, Roswell, Cumming and much of Forsyth County. It answers plumbing emergencies 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

The service list covers drains and hydrojetting, leak detection and slab leaks, pipe repair and repiping, sewer line repair and trenchless replacement, gas lines, sump and well pumps, toilets, sinks, showers, garbage disposals, water treatment and tank and tankless water heaters. The team notes that many local homes built from the mid-1980s to late 1990s have aging copper lines prone to pinhole leaks.
Jobs are quoted at a flat rate before work begins and backed by a satisfaction guarantee. Its punctuality guarantee pays customers $5 per minute late, up to $300.
tips: Ask for the flat-rate price before work starts.
Call any time for emergencies.
Older homes with copper lines may benefit from a plumbing inspection.

about: Good Ol'Boys Plumbing has served Alpharetta homes and businesses for more than 15 years, with a focus on plumbing repair and water heater service. The company handles everything from leaky faucets, toilets and hose bibs to burst pipes, leak detection and underground water and main line repairs.

Water heaters are a specialty, whether a unit needs repair or it is time for a replacement or upgrade. Technicians are typically available for same-day or next-day emergency calls, and the company backs its workmanship with a satisfaction guarantee.
Its service area includes Alpharetta, Cumming, Johns Creek, Milton and Roswell. Hours run from 6am to 8pm, and scheduled appointments can be booked by calling (678) 954-7611.
tips: Call early; same-day and next-day slots are common.
Ask about water heater replacement options.
Book within service hours of 6am to 8pm.

name: Zippy Plumber
desc: Underground plumbing, sewer lines and camera inspections.
about: Zippy Plumber specializes in underground and exterior plumbing for homes and commercial properties in Alpharetta and north metro Atlanta. Rather than indoor fixtures, its crews focus on the lines running from the building to the street, including sewer lines, water service lines and cleanouts.

Most jobs begin with a sewer camera inspection or leak detection to pinpoint the problem. From there the team uses hydro jetting to clear roots and buildup, and trenchless methods such as pipe lining and pipe bursting to limit digging, with targeted open-cut repairs when needed.

Crews coordinate 811 utility locates, follow trench safety rules and document work with video and written plans. Commercial clients include restaurants, retail centers, offices and multifamily properties.
tips: Start with a camera inspection to locate the issue.
Ask whether trenchless repair is an option for your line.
Call 404-989-2110 if you notice wet spots or sewer odors in the yard.

name: Hall Family Dental Care

New patients are welcome. The office files insurance claims for patients, accepts major credit cards and offers an online bill pay option. For patients without dental insurance, an in-house dental savings plan is available.

Patients can request appointments online or call (770) 751-0650, and the website posts hours and a map for finding the right building within the office complex. Some reviews posted on the practice's site come from families who have been patients there for years.
tips: Ask about the dental savings plan if you do not have insurance.
Request an appointment online or by phone.
Look for Building A, Suite 540, when you arrive.

The office is in network with most PPO dental insurance plans and offers a complimentary benefits check. Patients unsure about a diagnosis can schedule a no-obligation second opinion.

For patients without insurance, the Smile Makers Club membership includes two cleanings, exams and needed X-rays each year with no waiting periods or deductibles, plus discounts on other treatment. Regular hours are Monday through Friday 8am to 5pm, and Saturday appointments are available.
tips: Call for a free insurance benefits check before your visit.
Ask about the Smile Makers Club if you are uninsured.
Request a Saturday appointment if weekdays are hard.

Care spans routine preventive visits through more involved restorative work. The office places dental implants, makes crowns, bridges, porcelain onlays and full or partial dentures, and performs root canals and extractions, including wisdom teeth. Cosmetic options include Invisalign, porcelain veneers, bonding, whitening and full smile makeovers, and the practice also treats TMJ and TMD problems and describes itself as mercury-free.

Hours lean early in the week, with a 7am start on Tuesdays and a short Friday that ends at 1pm. New patients can call or request a visit through the scheduling form on the website, and the office lists CareCredit and other financing options for treatment that insurance does not cover.
tips: Tuesday opens at 7am, which helps if you need an appointment before work
Fridays end at 1pm, so book weekday afternoons Monday through Thursday
Uninsured new patients should ask about the new-patient exam and cleaning offer listed on the website

Directory listings describe a family-oriented practice in a modern facility, offering cleanings, fillings, crowns, bridges, teeth whitening and dental implants, alongside other cosmetic and restorative treatment.

That range means one office can handle routine checkups for the whole family as well as larger restorative work for adults, such as replacing a missing tooth or repairing a damaged one, and cosmetic requests like whitening. If you are new to the practice, ask what a first appointment includes when you call.

The appeal for many families is having most services in one place. Beyond exams, ultrasonic cleanings, fillings and bonding, the team handles porcelain crowns, bridges and inlays, dental implants, simple extractions and TMJ therapy. Cosmetic work includes veneers, Zoom whitening and ClearCorrect clear aligners, and the office uses digital imaging. Listings also mention orthodontic and oral surgery services.

As the name suggests, implant dentistry is a central focus, with full-arch implant treatment for patients replacing many teeth. The practice also offers comprehensive family dentistry, root canal treatment, Invisalign and other clear aligners, and cosmetic dentistry. Providers listed for the group include Dr. Lyda Harandifassih, DDS, and Dr. Shahrokh Bagheri, MD, DMD.

Cosmetic options include teeth whitening, porcelain veneers, Invisalign and dental implants. It also offers sleep apnea and TMJ care, mouthguards and night guards, sports dentistry and emergency visits.

The office puts a strong focus on comfort for nervous patients, with nitrous oxide, oral conscious sedation and IV sedation available, along with care for patients with a strong gag reflex. The posted schedule includes early 7am starts on Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday. The practice offers an in-house membership plan for patients without dental insurance, and appointments can be requested online or by phone.
tips: Early 7am appointments are listed for Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday.
Ask about sedation options if dental visits make you anxious.

CEREC technology allows single-visit crowns, and the practice handles bridges, implants, endodontics, periodontal deep cleanings and prosthodontics. Treatment for TMJ disorders and sleep apnea is offered too, and the office uses digital X-rays.

Weekday hours vary: Tuesdays and Wednesdays start at 7am, Thursdays at 9am, and Fridays close at 1pm. The office is closed on weekends. Most insurance is accepted, along with major cards and CareCredit.
tips: Ask about CEREC if you want a crown finished in a single visit
Tuesday and Wednesday 7am slots suit early risers
Spanish-speaking patients can request help in Spanish

Its long hours are the main draw for busy families. Weekday hours begin at 6:30am and run into the evening, and the hospital is also open on weekends, though published closing times vary between sources. Appointments can be booked through the practice's mobile app.

Services include wellness exams, vaccinations, puppy and kitten care, allergy management and sick visits. The clinic has in-house X-ray and ultrasound, offers laser therapy and virtual consultations, and sells wellness plans that bundle routine care.

Convenience is a big part of the model. Sick pets can be seen as walk-ins, and there is online booking and a waitlist for scheduled visits. Payment plans are available, and Spanish-speaking staff are on hand.
tips: Join the online waitlist before heading over for a sick visit
Ask about wellness plans if you have a new puppy or kitten

name: Midway Animal Hospital

about: Midway Animal Hospital opened on Atlanta Highway in 1988, founded by Dr. Rod Hardee with the goal of giving small animals the same standard of care people expect for themselves. It began in a small renovated house and has since grown into a three-story building with a staff of about 20, including four veterinarians.

The hospital has its own surgery center and in-house lab and diagnostic equipment, so many tests and procedures happen on site. Boarding, grooming and bathing are also offered, which lets families handle checkups, care and stays in one place.

Many clients have stayed with the practice for more than two decades. Tours are available for current and prospective clients who want to see the facility, and visitors may meet one of the resident cats.

Pets with allergies, skin problems, heart disease, cancer or chronic pain can be seen here, and laser therapy and nutrition counseling are available. Puppy, kitten and senior care programs round it out.

The hospital is open six days a week, with longer hours until 6pm on Mondays and Wednesdays and Saturday hours until 4pm. It is closed on Sundays. CareCredit, credit cards and pet insurance are accepted.

The hospital focuses on general veterinary medicine for dogs and cats. Wellness exams and preventive care sit alongside diagnostics, surgery and pet dentistry, including oral exams, cleanings and extractions. That makes it a practical choice for families who want one clinic to handle routine visits and most procedures.

New clients have been offered a discount on a first wellness exam, so ask about current offers when you call. The practice is well reviewed by local pet owners, and booking ahead is the best way to secure a time that fits your schedule.

Schedule dental cleanings ahead, since they need a planned drop-off
Bring previous vaccine records to your first visit

The hospital aims to care for pets at every life stage, from puppies and kittens to seniors and pets with chronic conditions. Routine services include wellness exams, vaccinations, dental care and diagnostic imaging. Dr. Gholston also performs orthopedic surgery, including TPLO repair for dogs with knee ligament injuries. Dr. Elizabeth Prince, who focuses on internal medicine and senior pets, is also on the team.
It serves Milton, Crabapple, Roswell and greater Alpharetta, and grocery-anchored parking in the plaza makes drop-offs easy.

Most specialty visits start with a referral from a regular veterinarian, who can send records ahead so the specialist has the full history. Emergency patients can come in any time, and calling on the way helps the team prepare.

Call on the way in during an emergency
Bring a list of your pet's current medications

No appointment is needed. A veterinarian sees your pet right away, before paperwork, and owners can stay with their pet throughout the visit. Staff will meet you at your car if you need help getting an animal inside. You can also call at any hour to talk with a doctor about whether a visit is needed.

The team treats dogs and cats as well as birds, reptiles and other exotic pets. Services include emergency and urgent care, surgery, endoscopy, ultrasound and X-rays, diagnostics, hospitalization and end-of-life care.

Routine service and repairs are the core of the business, but enthusiasts also come here for brake and suspension upgrades, performance work, race preparation and track tech inspections. The shop also handles interior and convertible top repairs, and it offers Noelle Performance software upgrades for some models.

Repairs use original equipment quality parts and carry a 12-month or 12,000-mile warranty. The shop is open weekdays from 8am to 6pm and closed on weekends. Members of the BMW Car Club of America and the Porsche Club of America can ask about club discounts.

about: Eurofed Automotive's Alpharetta shop sits in Suite B at 11090 Old Roswell Road and focuses on European vehicles, including BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Audi, Volkswagen, Porsche, Volvo and MINI. It is one of a group of Eurofed shops around the region.

ASE-certified technicians handle everything from factory-interval maintenance to complex diagnostics and repairs, using OEM parts and dealer-level diagnostic equipment. Digital vehicle inspections let customers see photos and notes on what the car needs before approving work, which helps when deciding what to fix now and what can wait.

The shop keeps weekday hours, 8am to 5pm Monday through Friday, and is closed on weekends. It is a practical option for European car owners in the Old Roswell Road and Mansell area who want specialist care outside a dealership.

The service list is long, covering brakes, oil changes, batteries, starters and alternators, transmission and clutch work, heating and air conditioning, alignments, timing belts, scheduled factory maintenance, emissions diagnostics and used car evaluations. about: 4A Auto A/C & Repair is a veteran-owned, father-and-son auto repair business serving Alpharetta, Johns Creek and nearby north Atlanta communities. Rather than asking you to drop a car at a shop, the team comes to your home or workplace.

As the name suggests, car air conditioning is a specialty, with leak detection, refrigerant recharging and repair. The team also handles electrical diagnostics, warning lights, battery and starting problems, brakes, cooling systems, ignition service and timing belt work, along with pre-purchase inspections on used cars. The business emphasizes structured testing so repairs address the actual cause.
Service runs Monday through Saturday, and the business is closed on Sundays. Calling or texting is the easiest way to describe the problem and set a time for a visit.

It says its technicians are not paid on quotas or commissions, so recommendations focus on what the car needs, and it emphasizes clear explanations of each repair.

Local customers rate the shop highly in online reviews. It keeps weekday hours, closing at 5:30pm, and is closed on weekends. The shop is about a quarter mile north of the Christian Brothers Automotive location on Atlanta Highway, which helps first-time visitors find it.

name: Import Auto Repair

It works on Audi, BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Porsche, Volkswagen, Volvo, Land Rover and more, including air suspension, DSG transmissions, coding and hybrid and EV repair.

The shop specializes in European cars, especially BMW, and also works on Audi, Mercedes-Benz, Porsche, Volkswagen, Volvo and Land Rover. Its capabilities include air suspension, DSG transmissions, module coding and programming, and hybrid and EV repair. The shop is part of a remote diagnostic network that gives its techs access to additional ASE master technicians on difficult problems.
Pre-purchase inspections are available for anyone shopping for a used European car, and repeat customers can join a rewards program. The shop is closed on weekends.

name: 1858 Athletic Club

Nutrition coaching is also offered, so the club suits people who want a structured plan rather than just open gym access. Training programs are personalized, and the club leans on a community atmosphere to keep members coming back.

name: Strength Society GA

address: 970 N Point Dr, Suite A100, Alpharetta, GA 30022

about: Strength Society is a boutique small-group strength gym in Suite A100 at 970 North Point Drive. It was founded by former NFL player Jonotthan Harrison, and its motto is There's Strength in Numbers, reflecting a team-style training culture.

Classes are capped at 12 members with two coaches each, which keeps form coaching close. Programming rotates through endurance, hypertrophy and power phases and mixes functional training, free weights, circuits and conditioning. Every movement can be scaled, so beginners and experienced lifters can share a class, and one-on-one coaching is available for people who want individual programming.

Classes run from 5:30am on weekdays, with midday and evening options on some days and a couple of Saturday morning sessions. The gym is closed Sundays. Booking ahead is required, and the facility has showers, parking and accessible restrooms.

name: CORE57
desc: Fitness and nutrition coaching studio at Alpharetta City Center offering one-on-one personal training, semi-private sessions and group classes that mix strength, mobility, cardio and interval work. The program emphasizes education and sustainable habits, and the studio also sells performance wear and hosts community events.
tips: Try a semi-private session for coaching at a lower cost than one-on-one
Start with a fitness assessment to set goals
Check the front shop for performance wear
about: CORE57 is a fitness and nutrition coaching studio at 394 Commerce Street in Alpharetta City Center. Founder Kolleen Riddick Losch opened it in late 2018 as an expansion of her earlier business, Core Physique. The name refers to the studio's five steps to success and seven foundations of fitness.

Clients can book one-on-one personal training, semi-private sessions or group classes that mix strength, mobility, cardio, high-intensity circuits, TRX and yoga-inspired work. Fitness assessments, goal setting and nutrition guidance are part of the program, with an emphasis on education and habits that last.
The studio also sells performance wear and hosts community events. Its Alpharetta City Center location puts it within walking distance of downtown restaurants and shops.
hours: Mon 5:45am-7:30pm; Tue-Wed 6am-6:30pm; Thu 6am-7:30pm; Fri 5:45am-2pm; Sat 7am-12pm; Sun 1pm-2pm

about: Horsepower Fitness is a boutique training gym in Suite 120 at 12640 Crabapple Road, a short walk from Milton City Hall in the Crabapple area. It focuses on small-group and one-on-one personal training rather than open gym memberships.

Sessions blend strength and conditioning with functional and free-weight training, and the gym also offers HYROX race preparation and nutrition coaching. That mix makes it a fit both for people building general strength and for those training toward a specific event.

Weekday sessions run from 5:30am into the early evening, with a short Saturday morning window, and the gym is closed Sundays. Reservations are required. Amenities include showers, a changing room, towels and on-site parking.
tips: Book sessions in advance, since walk-ins are not the model
Ask about HYROX training if you are preparing for a race

name: Alpha Strength & Power Gym

It caters to strength athletes and members focused on conditioning and muscle development from Alpharetta and nearby north Atlanta communities.

Ask how to book on-site massage therapy.

Directory listings describe it as a full-service gym built around structured training programs that help members build strength, improve conditioning and work toward specific fitness goals.

Listed services include strength training, group fitness classes and on-site massage therapy for recovery. The emphasis on programming makes it a fit for strength athletes and for members who want a planned approach to conditioning and muscle development rather than casual open-gym time. It draws members from Alpharetta and nearby north Atlanta communities.

No official website could be found, so details such as class schedules, membership options and how massage appointments are booked could not be verified. Call before visiting to ask about hours, what a first visit looks like and which programs suit your experience level.

Members choose among one-on-one personal training, semi-private training and group HIIT classes, including a hybrid HIIT format of about 40 minutes. Coaches build customized workout plans and pair them with nutrition help and regular accountability check-ins, and the program is built to work for both beginners and experienced athletes.

First-timers are asked to arrive 10 minutes early to check in and get a tour. Bring athletic clothes, shoes and water. Showers, towels and mats are provided, so it is easy to head straight to work afterward, and there is parking on site.

name: Alloy Personal Training
desc: Personal training gym at Haynes Bridge Village from Alloy, a brand with more than 30 years in customized training. Members get one-on-one sessions, small group classes, nutrition coaching and results tracking, all aimed at people who want structured accountability and measurable progress.

The gym focuses on coached workouts rather than open access. Members can choose one-on-one personal training or small group sessions, with programs customized to their experience level. Nutrition coaching and results tracking are part of the offer, making it a fit for busy professionals who want accountability and measurable progress.
Weekday hours run from 8am into the evening Monday through Thursday, with a slightly earlier close on Fridays. Reach out to set up an introductory session and assessment before committing.

name: Club Pilates Avalon
desc: Reformer Pilates studio at Avalon with group classes for all levels.
about: Club Pilates at Avalon is a reformer Pilates studio at 7160 Avalon Way, inside the Avalon shopping and dining district. Classes are low-impact, full-body workouts that put a modern spin on classical Pilates.

Group classes use Balanced Body reformers along with other equipment such as Bosu balls, TRX, EXO-Chairs, barres, weights and springboards. Classes are offered at many times through the day, and private training is available too. The focus is core strength, flexibility, coordination and mind-body connection, and classes are offered at different levels.
The studio lists hours from 6am to 8pm daily. New students can start with a free intro class, which is the easiest way to learn the reformer before joining regular classes.

Early 6am classes help you fit Pilates in before work

desc: Boutique yoga studio on South Main Street, part of Lift Yoga + Body with studios in Dunwoody and Johns Creek. Classes range from restorative, yin and meditation to power, vinyasa and hot yoga plus Fit Pilates, with workshops and private sessions, all in an inclusive setting for every age and level.
