The menu also covers crab wontons, pork dumplings served pan fried or steamed, egg rolls and spring rolls, plus entrees such as Chang's Spicy Chicken, Kung Pao Chicken, Mongolian Beef, Ma Po Tofu and Crispy Honey Shrimp, along with noodle and rice dishes and gluten free options.

The location offers patio dining, free Wi-Fi, happy hour, large party bookings, catering and delivery or takeout. On Wednesdays it runs Wine Wednesdays with half off bottles of wine and champagne. Self parking is available near the restaurant.
tips: Go on a Wednesday for half off bottles of wine and champagne.
Ask about gluten free versions of dishes when you order.
Book ahead for large groups, which the restaurant takes reservations for.

name: Chin Chin Chinese Restaurant
desc: Family run Chinese restaurant on Rucker Road, part of a metro Atlanta group serving since 1994, with a glass enclosed kitchen and gluten free and MSG free options.
about: Chin Chin Chinese Restaurant has served Chinese cuisine in metro Atlanta since 1994, and its Alpharetta location is at 270 Rucker Road, Suite 115. The group's other restaurant is on Peachtree Road in Brookhaven. Chin Chin says it received several Creative Loafing awards of excellence between 1998 and 2020.

The menu runs from mild to spicy and light to rich, and diners can watch the chefs cook through a glass enclosed kitchen. Gluten free and MSG free options are available on request. Reviews posted on the restaurant's site mention the fried dumplings, beef curry rolls, sweet and sour chicken and eggplant, along with a good vegetarian selection.
The Alpharetta location is open every day from 11am to 10pm for dine in, and the restaurant also offers online ordering for takeout and delivery.
tips: Ask for the gluten free or MSG free versions of dishes.
Sit where you can watch the cooks work in the glass enclosed kitchen.
Order online ahead for faster takeout.

name: Iron Age Korean Steak House
desc: All you can eat Korean barbecue at Halcyon where guests grill bulgogi and other meats at tabletop grills, with refillable sides and staff guidance.
about: Iron Age Korean Steak House at Halcyon offers a do it yourself Korean barbecue experience in the Halcyon development off McGinnis Ferry Road. Iron Age opened in 2008 as metro Atlanta's first all you can eat Korean barbecue restaurant, and the Duluth based brand also has locations in Sandy Springs, Kennesaw and Toco Hills, plus Maryland, Virginia and Thailand.

Guests cook beef bulgogi, other marinated meats and vegetables at built in tabletop grills, and staff help with cooking times and food or allergy questions. Side dishes are refilled when you set an empty dish at the edge of the table.

Seating is first come, first served and guests are asked to keep to a two hour dining time. Reservations are taken only for parties of 8 or more, booked at least 6 hours ahead, and tables are not guaranteed on weekends. It works well for birthdays and group dinners.
tips: Parties of 8 or more should reserve at least 6 hours ahead.
Plan on a two hour table limit.
Set an empty side dish at the table edge to get a refill.

name: Bonchon Alpharetta
desc: Korean fried chicken spot on Old Milton Parkway serving double fried wings and drumsticks in signature sauces, plus bulgogi, udon, dumplings and Korean comfort food.
about: Bonchon Alpharetta is the Korean fried chicken chain's location at 4055 Old Milton Parkway. Bonchon means "my hometown" in Korean, and the brand describes itself as a family friendly, casual restaurant built around crunchy double fried chicken.

The chicken comes in signature sauces such as Soy Garlic and Spicy. The rest of the menu leans on Korean comfort food and Asian fusion dishes, including K-Fire Chicken in a buldak style spicy sauce with mozzarella, Bulgogi Stir-Fry Udon, Bacon Kimchi Stir-Fry Udon, manduguk dumpling soup, potstickers, cheese balls and Korean cucumber salad.

The restaurant is open for dine in, takeout and online ordering every day. On Mondays and Tuesdays it runs a $1 wings special for dine in guests, limited to 15 wings per order or table. Note that many sauces contain sesame.
tips: Visit Monday or Tuesday for the dine in $1 wings special.
Order Soy Garlic if you want flavor without much heat.
Mention sesame allergies, since many dishes contain sesame.
address: 4055 Old Milton Pkwy, Ste 12, Alpharetta, GA 30005

name: Taco Mac Old Milton
desc: Taco Mac's Old Milton Parkway sports bar pairs wings and burgers with a long, rotating craft beer list, open late every night for game watching.
about: Taco Mac Old Milton is the Atlanta born sports bar chain's location at 4305 Old Milton Parkway. It is a go to spot for watching games over wings, burgers and the brand's other bar food favorites, and it stays open until midnight most nights and 1am on Fridays and Saturdays.

Craft beer is a big part of the draw. The location's live tap list on Taco Mac's site tracked 73 unique beers in 20 styles when we checked, from domestic lagers to Georgia IPAs, ciders and stouts. Beer fans can join Taco Mac's Brewniversity program, which rewards trying new beers.
The dining room is open, and takeout, delivery, online ordering and catering are available. A lunch menu is offered as well.
tips: Check the live tap list on the location page before you go.
Join Brewniversity if you plan to work through the beer list.
Order catering for game day parties at home.
address: 4305 Old Milton Pkwy, Ste 101, Alpharetta, GA 30022

name: Wild Wing Cafe Alpharetta
desc: Wings and live music on Windward Parkway, with 33 wing sauces, burgers, big screens for sports and a dog friendly patio, plus local DJs and bands most weekends.
about: Wild Wing Cafe Alpharetta is at 5530 Windward Parkway and is one of the chain's Georgia locations. Chicken wings are the focus, with 33 sauces that range from sweet BBQ and the teriyaki style Ginger to the Reaper and Braveheart, the hottest sauce on the menu.

Beyond wings, the menu includes burgers such as the Ultimate Bacon Cheeseburger, Hot Shots, fried mushrooms, grilled chicken salads with house made dressings, soups and a Wild Child menu for kids. The bar runs a happy hour, and big screens carry the major games in every season.
Local DJs and bands play nearly every weekend, and the outdoor patio is dog friendly. Dine in, takeout, curbside pickup, online ordering and catering are all offered.
tips: Check the event calendar for weekend live music.
Bring your dog to the outdoor patio.
Try a mild sauce like Ginger or Wild West before the hottest ones.

name: Cherry Street Brewpub at Halcyon
desc: Craft brewery and restaurant at Halcyon with 20 house beers on tap, a full bar, weekend brunch, a beer garden with live music and a 21 and up brewhouse.
about: Cherry Street Brewpub at Halcyon is the Alpharetta brewery and restaurant from Cherry Street Brewing, which calls itself the original Forsyth County brewery and has brewed for 13 years. Its other brewpub is at Vickery Village in Cumming.

The Halcyon brewpub has two bars with 20 craft beers on tap, a restaurant side and a 21 and up bar space called the Brewhouse. The kitchen serves lunch and dinner with appetizers, handhelds and entrees, a kids menu and brunch on Saturdays and Sundays. The bar also pours craft cocktails, frozen drinks and a range of bourbons, and beers can go to walk around Halcyon's open container district.

Weekly events include Twisted Trivia on Mondays at 7:30pm, kids eat free on Tuesday evenings with an adult entree, and live music in the beer garden on Thursdays. Same day reservations are not accepted.
tips: Call ahead to reserve for Monday trivia in the Brewhouse.
Bring kids on Tuesday, 5pm to 9pm, when one kids meal is free per adult entree.
Reserve at least a day ahead, since same day reservations are not taken.

name: Carrie's Restaurant and Bar
desc: Patio bar and restaurant inside The Hamilton hotel in downtown Alpharetta, serving weekend brunch, lunch, daily social hour and dinner with indoor and outdoor seating.
about: Carrie's Restaurant and Bar is the restaurant and patio bar at The Hamilton Alpharetta, a Curio Collection by Hilton boutique hotel at 35 Milton Avenue in downtown Alpharetta. The hotel describes it as a place for light fare and drinks, with both indoor and outdoor seating.

Brunch runs Saturday and Sunday from 11am to 2pm. On weekdays Carrie's serves lunch from 11am to 2pm, and every day it has a social hour from 2pm to 5pm. Dinner is served Monday through Saturday from 5pm to 10pm and Sunday until 9pm. The menus include cocktails, wine by the bottle and desserts.
The bar stays open until 11pm Monday through Thursday and midnight on Fridays and Saturdays. Reservations can be made through the hotel's dining page or by calling the hotel.
tips: Book ahead for weekend brunch, which runs 11am to 2pm.
Stop in from 2pm to 5pm for the daily social hour.
Pick a patio table on mild days.
hours: Bar Mon-Thu 11am-11pm; Fri-Sat 11am-12am; Sun 12:30pm-10pm; brunch Sat-Sun 11am-2pm

name: Ocean & Acre
desc: Bright, barn-like restaurant at Halcyon pairing smoked meats and seasonal produce with shareable seafood and a raw bar.
about: Ocean & Acre is one of the anchor sit-down restaurants at Halcyon, the walkable district at GA 400 exit 12. It sits in a bright, barn-like building and builds its menu around two ideas: seafood from the ocean and smoked meats and seasonal produce from the land. Expect shareable plates, a raw bar and entrees that work as well for a business lunch as for a weekend dinner with friends.

The restaurant is open every day from 11am, until 10pm Monday through Saturday and 9pm on Sunday. Weekday happy hour runs 3pm to 6pm, weekend brunch is served 11am to 3pm, and a live musician usually plays on Sunday afternoons from 1pm to 4pm.
Parking is free in the Halcyon deck a short walk away. After dinner, the Village Green, Kilwins and the Big Creek Greenway trailhead are all within a few minutes on foot.
tips: Come for weekday happy hour from 3pm to 6pm.
Sunday brunch comes with live music from 1pm to 4pm.
Book ahead for Friday and Saturday dinner.

name: Cattle Shed Wine & Steak Bar
desc: Halcyon's special-occasion pick from the owners of HOBNOB, with premium steaks, seafood, charcuterie and more than 200 wines.
about: Cattle Shed Wine & Steak Bar comes from the same owners as HOBNOB Neighborhood Tavern and takes its inspiration from Charleston. The menu centers on premium steaks and seafood, with charcuterie and cheese boards for the table, and the bar pours more than 200 wines along with wine-infused cocktails.

It is open daily from 11am, until 10pm Tuesday through Saturday and 9pm on Sunday and Monday. Happy hour runs every day from 2:30pm to 6pm, and weekend brunch is served from 11am to 4pm. Weekly specials have included a chef's cut steak dinner for $38 on Mondays, wine flights on Tuesdays and half off select bottles of wine on Wednesdays.
It is the Halcyon restaurant locals pick for anniversaries, birthdays and client dinners, and it fills up on weekend nights. Free parking is in the Halcyon deck.
tips: Monday is the night for the $38 chef's cut steak dinner.
Daily happy hour runs 2:30pm to 6pm.
Reserve ahead for weekend dinners.

name: Eclipse di Luna
desc: Spanish tapas restaurant at Halcyon with paella, empanadas, patatas bravas, sangria and live music most nights.
about: Eclipse di Luna is a longtime Atlanta tapas name with a location at Halcyon. The menu covers Spanish small-plate favorites such as paella, empanadas and patatas bravas, plus a daily fresh fish special, and pitchers of sangria are a big part of the experience.

Live music is the other draw. The weekly schedule has included flamenco on Monday evenings, a band on Tuesdays, flamenco guitar on Saturday and Sunday afternoons, salsa and merengue on Saturday night and a late DJ set after 10:30pm on Saturdays. Weekday happy hour runs 4pm to 6pm.
It stays open until midnight on Friday and Saturday, making it one of Halcyon's later options. Monday service starts at 4pm, and the rest of the week it opens at 11am.
tips: Saturday night brings salsa and merengue, then a DJ.
Weekday happy hour is 4pm to 6pm.
Order a pitcher of sangria for the table.

name: HOBNOB Neighborhood Tavern
desc: Neighborhood tavern at Halcyon with a deep bourbon list, blended burgers, weekend brunch, trivia, live music and kids eat free nights.
about: HOBNOB Neighborhood Tavern covers lunch, dinner and weekend brunch at Halcyon with a deep bourbon list and burgers made from a short rib, brisket and chuck blend. It is a reliable place to watch a game, and the same owners run Cattle Shed Wine & Steak Bar across the property.

The weekly calendar keeps it busy: a $13 beer and burger deal on Mondays, a taco and margarita special on Tuesdays, featured whiskey on Wednesdays, ladies night and music bingo on Thursdays, and live music on Friday and Saturday at 8pm. Kids eat free Sunday through Thursday, and weekday happy hour runs 3pm to 6pm.
Each holiday season HOBNOB opens The Elf Upstairs pop-up bar and hosts Brunch with the Grinch, which sells out early.
tips: Kids eat free Sunday through Thursday.
Live music starts at 8pm on Fridays and Saturdays.
Book Brunch with the Grinch early in December.

name: Char Pizzeria
desc: Artisanal pizza spot at Halcyon, an easy casual lunch or dinner near the Village Green.
about: Char Pizzeria is Halcyon's dedicated pizza restaurant, turning out artisanal pies for a casual lunch or a family dinner. It sits on Halcyon Way near the Market Hall and the Village Green, so it is an easy choice when you have kids in tow or want something quick before a walk on the Big Creek Greenway.

It is open every day from 11am, until 9pm Sunday through Thursday and 10pm on Friday and Saturday. Takeout works well too, and Halcyon keeps 15-minute curbside spots for to-go pickups so you do not have to park in the deck for a quick grab.
If your group cannot agree on pizza, the Market Hall next door has dumplings, poke, salads and Mediterranean food, and Kilwins is close by for dessert.
tips: Use Halcyon's 15-minute curbside spots for takeout.
Take slices to the Village Green on a nice evening.
Open until 10pm on Fridays and Saturdays.

name: Never Enough Thyme
desc: Family-owned comfort food restaurant that started in Alpharetta, with homemade cooking and weekend brunch at Halcyon.
about: Never Enough Thyme is a family-owned restaurant that got its start in Alpharetta and is known for homemade comfort food. Its Halcyon location gives the district a casual, everyday option between the bigger chef-driven dining rooms, good for a weeknight dinner or lunch with the kids.

Weekend brunch runs from 10am to 2pm on Saturday and Sunday. Otherwise it opens at 11am, closing at 8pm Monday through Thursday and on Sunday, and at 9pm on Friday and Saturday, which makes it one of the earlier-closing restaurants at Halcyon.
Free parking is in the Halcyon deck, and the Village Green is a short walk away for kids who need to run around after the meal.
tips: Weekend brunch starts at 10am.
It closes at 8pm most weeknights, so go early.
A good pick for an easygoing family dinner.

name: Gu's Dumplings
desc: Halcyon outpost of the well-known Atlanta Szechuan restaurant, serving dumplings, noodles and stir-fry in the Market Hall.
about: Gu's Dumplings is the Halcyon outpost of a well-known Atlanta Szechuan restaurant family, and it is one of the most popular stops in Halcyon's Market Hall. The menu focuses on dumplings, noodles and stir-fry, with the numbing, spicy Szechuan flavors the brand is known for alongside milder choices.

It is closed on Mondays. From Tuesday through Sunday it opens at 11am, closing at 9pm most nights and 10pm on Friday and Saturday. Ordering is quick, which makes it a favorite for lunch, and seating is in the Market Hall and around the Village Green.
The Market Hall also has public restrooms, family restrooms and an ATM, and the other stalls make it easy for a group with different cravings to eat together.
tips: Closed Mondays.
Ask which dishes are the spiciest before ordering.
Eat on the Village Green when the weather is nice.

name: Il Bottegone
desc: Small Italian market in Halcyon's Market Hall with cheeses, cured meats, bread and custom charcuterie boards.
about: Il Bottegone is a small Italian market inside Halcyon's Market Hall. Shelves and cases hold imported cheeses, cured meats, bread and pantry items, and the counter makes custom charcuterie boards, which locals pick up for parties or carry out to the Village Green for a picnic.
It opens at 10:30am every day and closes at 8pm Monday through Thursday, 9pm on Friday and Saturday and 6pm on Sunday, so it is easy to stop in on the way home from work.
It pairs well with a bottle from Rise & Wine across the property, and it is a handy last-minute stop for host gifts during the holidays.
tips: Order a charcuterie board ahead for a party.
Pair it with a bottle from Rise & Wine.
Closes at 6pm on Sundays.

name: X-Golf Georgia
desc: Halcyon's indoor golf simulator and sports bar, with bays for practice, lessons and group outings plus a full bar.
about: X-Golf at Halcyon is an indoor golf simulator venue with a sports bar attached. Bays work for solo practice, lessons, a round with friends or a company outing, and the simulators let you play well-known courses in any weather, which makes it a popular rainy-day and winter plan.

It is open 10am to 10pm Monday through Saturday and 10am to 6pm on Sunday. The bar serves cocktails, beer and shareable appetizers, and weekly specials have included $5 margaritas on Mondays and $6 Tito's cocktails on Tuesdays.
Groups should book bays ahead, especially on Friday and Saturday nights. Parking is free in the Halcyon deck, and the restaurants on Town Square are steps away for dinner afterward.
tips: Reserve a bay ahead for weekend nights.
Sunday hours end at 6pm.
A good rainy-day plan with older kids.

name: Trader Joe's Halcyon
desc: The Trader Joe's that anchors Halcyon's shopping, open daily from 9am to 9pm.
about: Trader Joe's anchors the shopping at Halcyon and is the reason many south Forsyth and north Alpharetta neighbors stop by every week. The store carries the chain's private-label groceries, frozen meals, snacks, flowers and wine.

It is open every day from 9am to 9pm. Weekend mornings and weekday evenings after work are the busiest times, and the lot can fill on Saturdays, so the free Halcyon parking deck is often the easier choice.
Pair a grocery run with coffee at BRASH, a charcuterie stop at Il Bottegone or a walk on the Big Creek Greenway, whose trailhead is near Halcyon Way and Ronald Reagan Parkway.
tips: Shop weekday mornings for shorter lines.
Use the free deck if the lot is full.
Grab flowers here for a quick gift.

name: Rise & Wine
desc: Husband-and-wife wine market overlooking Halcyon's Village Green, with weekday happy hours and themed tasting nights.
about: Rise & Wine is a husband-and-wife wine market that overlooks Halcyon's Village Green. You can shop bottles to take home or sit down for a glass, and it has become a relaxed meeting spot for neighbors before or after dinner on the property.

Weekday happy hour runs 4pm to 7pm with themed nights such as Tasty Tuesday, Wine Down Wednesday and Thirsty Thursday, and Wednesdays have included a free 187 mL bottle with a $25 purchase. It is closed on Mondays.
Pair a bottle with a charcuterie board from Il Bottegone in the Market Hall, or ask the owners for a recommendation for a host gift.
tips: Closed Mondays.
Weekday happy hour is 4pm to 7pm.
Ask the owners to pick a bottle for a gift.

name: Kilwins Halcyon
desc: Ice cream, fudge and chocolate shop at Halcyon, the classic dessert stop after dinner on the property.
about: Kilwins at Halcyon is the district's go-to dessert stop for ice cream, fudge, caramel apples and chocolates. It is a natural last stop after dinner at one of Halcyon's restaurants or an afternoon on the Village Green with the kids.
It is open daily from 11am, until 9pm Sunday through Thursday and 10pm on Friday and Saturday. Lines can stretch out the door on warm weekend evenings, so plan on a short wait.
Boxed chocolates and fudge make easy gifts during the holidays. Kilwins also has a shop in Downtown Alpharetta on Market Street.
tips: Expect a line on warm weekend nights.
Boxed fudge makes an easy holiday gift.
Walk your scoop over to the Village Green.

name: BRASH Coffee Halcyon
desc: Atlanta coffee roaster's Halcyon cafe, open daily from 8am to 4pm.
about: BRASH Coffee Roasters is an Atlanta-based roaster, and its Halcyon cafe is the district's main coffee stop. Expect espresso drinks, drip coffee and cold brew made from BRASH's own roasts, served to a mix of remote workers, parents and shoppers.

It is open every day from 8am to 4pm, so plan on a morning or early afternoon visit. Halcyon offers free Wi-Fi in the common areas on the Halcyon-Public network, and the Village Green is a good place to sit outside with your drink.
Pair a coffee with a grocery run at Trader Joe's or a morning walk on the Big Creek Greenway, whose trailhead is near Halcyon Way and Ronald Reagan Parkway.
tips: Open 8am to 4pm daily.
Take your coffee on a Big Creek Greenway walk.
Free Wi-Fi is on the Halcyon-Public network.

name: Embassy Suites Alpharetta Halcyon
desc: Hilton's all-suite hotel inside Halcyon, steps from the restaurants, shops and Big Creek Greenway.
about: Embassy Suites by Hilton Alpharetta Halcyon is the hotel inside the Halcyon district, a Hilton all-suite property on Market Street. Staying here puts you within walking distance of Halcyon's restaurants, Trader Joe's, X-Golf and the Village Green, and a few minutes from GA 400 at exit 12.

It is a practical base for visiting family in south Forsyth or north Alpharetta, for youth sports weekends and for business travelers working along the GA 400 corridor. Avalon and Downtown Alpharetta are about 15 minutes south by car.
Book early for holiday weekends and big local events, when rooms near GA 400 fill up.
tips: Walk to dinner on Town Square.
Book early for holiday weekends.
Avalon is about 15 minutes south by car.

name: Caffè Antico
desc: Italian coffee bar at Avalon with espresso, gelato and light Italian bites, next to Antico Pizza.
about: Caffè Antico is the Italian coffee bar at Avalon from the team behind Antico Pizza. It serves espresso and cappuccino, gelato and light Italian food, and it is an easy stop before shopping or after a pizza dinner next door.
It is open daily from 10am, until 9pm Monday through Thursday, 10pm on Friday and Saturday and 8pm on Sunday, so it works for a morning coffee or an evening scoop.
In winter it is a short walk from Avalon on Ice, and gelato or a hot drink is a natural follow-up to a skate. Self-parking in the Avalon decks is free.
tips: Pair it with dinner at Antico Pizza.
Grab a hot drink after Avalon on Ice.
Open until 10pm on weekends.

name: Le Macaron French Pastries Avalon
desc: French macarons, pastries and gelato on the Boulevard at Avalon.
about: Le Macaron French Pastries is a French-style dessert shop on Avalon Boulevard, part of a franchise known for colorful macarons in a long list of flavors. It also sells pastries and other sweets, and boxes of macarons are a popular gift.
Hours are short on weekdays: it opens at 4pm Monday through Thursday and closes at 9pm, then opens at 11am on Friday and Saturday until 10pm and noon to 8pm on Sunday.
Pick up a box for a birthday or hostess gift, or pair a few macarons with coffee from one of the cafes nearby on the Boulevard.
tips: Weekday hours start at 4pm.
A box of macarons makes an easy gift.
Open until 10pm Friday and Saturday.

name: Gusto! Avalon
desc: Atlanta-born fast-casual spot at Avalon serving grilled bowls and wraps, open daily from 10:30am.
about: Gusto! is an Atlanta-born fast-casual restaurant, and its Avalon location is one of the quickest healthy meals on the Boulevard. The menu is built around grilled proteins served as bowls and wraps, with sauces and toppings you can mix to taste.
It is open every day from 10:30am to 9pm, so it works for a fast lunch between stores or an early dinner before a movie at Regal Avalon.
Orders move quickly, and takeout is easy if you would rather eat in the plaza. Self-parking in Avalon's decks is free.
tips: A fast lunch between stores.
Eat before a movie at Regal Avalon.
Open 10:30am to 9pm every day.

name: Posman Books Avalon
desc: Independent bookstore on the Boulevard at Avalon with new books, children's books and gifts.
about: Posman Books is an independent bookstore on Avalon Boulevard. Its Avalon shop carries new fiction and nonfiction, cookbooks, children's books and gifts, and it is an easy place to browse between stops on the Boulevard.
It is open Monday through Saturday from 10am to 9pm and Sunday from 10am to 6pm, roughly matching Avalon center hours.
It is a good stop with kids, and an easy place to find a last-minute gift during the holidays. Pair a browse with coffee or ice cream nearby on the Boulevard.
tips: Browse the children's books with little ones.
A good last-minute gift stop.
Sunday hours end at 6pm.

name: EVEN Hotel Alpharetta
desc: IHG's wellness-focused hotel on Old Milton Parkway next to Avalon.
about: EVEN Hotel Alpharetta is an IHG hotel on Old Milton Parkway next to Avalon. The EVEN brand focuses on wellness, with workout space and healthier food options, and it markets itself to guests visiting the Avalon area.

Its location makes it easy to walk or take a short ride to Avalon's restaurants, the Regal theater and Avalon on Ice in winter, while usually costing less than staying on the Boulevard itself. Downtown Alpharetta is about a mile away along the Alpha Loop.
Book early for big Avalon weekends such as the Lighting of Avalon in November and graduation season in May.
tips: Walk to Avalon restaurants.
Book early for the Lighting of Avalon weekend.
Downtown is about a mile away.
